title: HBO's Harry Potter embraces book-accurate 1990s costume design
body_md:
New promotional images from HBO's Harry Potter adaptation reveal an important difference between the television production and the earlier feature films. The costume department is embracing the early 1990s setting associated with the original books rather than simply reproducing the visual style established by the movies.

One recently released image shows Dominic McLaughlin as Harry during his first visit to Diagon Alley. Before acquiring his wizarding wardrobe, the character wears ordinary clothes that reflect the appearance of a child growing up during that period.

The franchise's official website has described how the costume team approached its research. Designers consulted family photographs and searched secondhand clothing sources to capture everyday fashion rather than relying exclusively on idealized representations of the decade. The objective is to make the ordinary world feel inhabited and recognizable before Harry encounters the extraordinary one.

The production is also exploring how magical society might develop a distinct relationship with fashion. Wizards and witches are not necessarily expected to follow mainstream clothing trends, and the costume department has embraced the possibility of unconventional combinations and individual styles.

That distinction could provide a useful visual shorthand for the cultural differences between the wizarding world and the nonmagical society surrounding it. Rather than giving every magical character a uniform appearance, costume design can communicate personality, background and attitudes toward the wider world.

The original Harry Potter films began in 2001 and concluded their principal series in 2011. Their costumes reflected, to varying degrees, the contemporary sensibilities of the period in which they were produced. HBO's decision to emphasize the books' earlier setting gives the new production an opportunity to establish a separate visual identity.

A period setting may also influence other aspects of the adaptation, including everyday objects, domestic environments and the contrast between Harry's upbringing and his introduction to magic. These are possibilities suggested by the creative approach rather than confirmation of specific scenes.

The longer television format could allow the adaptation to explore details that the feature films had limited time to include. Nevertheless, costume accuracy alone cannot establish whether the series will successfully capture the books' characters, themes or narrative structure.

Harry Potter is scheduled to premiere on HBO on December 25, 2026. When the series arrives, viewers will be able to assess whether this attention to period detail meaningfully enhances the story.

Do you prefer the new adaptation's early 1990s aesthetic, or the familiar look of the original films?
